integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

value: Automated review only, and not independent: no human security reviewer exists anywhere in this corpus, and the corpus has no security organisation.

The oracle review checked one thing and it is the thing the master prompt names: that each measure's expected outcome is derived from something other than the implementation's own output, and that each measure states which of the four oracle kinds it uses. Two measures declare source_grounded, one analytical_model and one synthetic_assumption, and each names what its oracle is not.
No measure was executed and no execution claims otherwise. All five execution records carry execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked' with the specific missing environment named.

This is not a penetration test and the review did not perform one. No exploit was developed, no advisory source was consulted, no vulnerability was scored. A threat in the TARA remains a static reading of code and this review does not change that.

The five security requirements themselves were NOT edited. Where a measure found a problem with a requirement - an unachievable criterion, a dangling reference - the problem became a finding and the requirement is unchanged.

dispositions.action: Not resolved. A measure with a weak oracle is better than a requirement with no verification plan at all, and the record says what the oracle cannot see. The advisory half needs an authorised party, which no part of this corpus can supply.

Correctly left open. The pre-existing findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12 were NOT edited to claim closure, because closure of a verification-evidence finding requires evidence and none exists. This is the single place in this pass where a tempting edit was declined.
Not resolved. Recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000028. No acceptance criterion was altered and no measure's expected outcome was softened to make it passable.

Not resolved. Neither available workaround was taken: the validator rule was not modified, and no verifies or validates link was authored with a requirement as its source. The gap between the link and the finding is deliberate and is recorded so that a reader who sees both does not conclude that one is wrong.

findings.description: One of the five security measures has no oracle available to it and uses the weakest oracle that can honestly be applied - distinctness rather than unpredictability, and a check on the record of an advisory check rather than on the advisories. The measure states this on its own face, and the finding that the advisory clause cannot be satisfied in this corpus at all is more serious than the measure's weakness.
findings.evidence: Read of FB2-VER-TMS-000020's oracle_detail. The 'days since last advisory check' expected outcome has no oracle because this corpus may not consult an advisory source; the measure's precondition list states that the last precondition is NOT satisfied.

findings.description: All five security executions are blocked, so the requirement's verification state moved from 'no measure at all' to 'measure authored, oracle declared, execution blocked'. The five pre-existing findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12 that asked for verification evidence remain open.
findings.evidence: Validator finding count before and after this pass: 21 findings before, 16 after, the five that disappeared being exactly the five 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link' findings against FB2-SAF-SEC-000001..000005. The link is now present; the evidence is not, and the pre-existing findings say so in their own resolution fields.

findings.description: The five security requirements now carry correctly directed verifies links and the validator still reports them as unverified, because the rule reads the link's source endpoint while the relation's documented direction puts the requirement at the target. 12 of the corpus's 21 standing findings come from this one defect.
findings.evidence: Read from docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py's _validate_semantic_rules, and confirmed on disk: each of FB2-SAF-SEC-000001..000005 is the target of a verifies link from FB2-VER-TMS-000016..000020 and the source of none. Recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000029.

findings.description: Two of the five measures assert an acceptance criterion that no correct implementation can meet, and record the requirement's own zero as the expected outcome rather than quietly relaxing it to something passable.
findings.evidence: FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 both state a zero-false-rejection criterion over 24 h on a channel carrying an integrity value. Recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000028 and named in both measures' oracle_detail.

record_verbatim.lifecycle_status_note: draft, not reviewed and not approved: this is the output of an automated pass and no human has confirmed it. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only and says nothing about engineering validity.
limitations: Automated review only, and not independent: no human security reviewer exists anywhere in this corpus, and the corpus has no security organisation.

The oracle review checked one thing and it is the thing the master prompt names: that each measure's expected outcome is derived from something other than the implementation's own output, and that each measure states which of the four oracle kinds it uses. Two measures declare source_grounded, one analytical_model and one synthetic_assumption, and each names what its oracle is not.
No measure was executed and no execution claims otherwise. All five execution records carry execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked' with the specific missing environment named.

This is not a penetration test and the review did not perform one. No exploit was developed, no advisory source was consulted, no vulnerability was scored. A threat in the TARA remains a static reading of code and this review does not change that.

The five security requirements themselves were NOT edited. Where a measure found a problem with a requirement - an unachievable criterion, a dangling reference - the problem became a finding and the requirement is unchanged.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-REV-000015` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
